subject: Airlocked artifact rotation & operator safety checklist
messages:
From: Sally Park <sally.park@edgecorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgecorp.com>, EdgeCorp Security <security@edgecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Airlock deployment — artifact rotation and operator access questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team reviewed the on-prem VPC plan and has a few open items before we sign off on an air-gapped deployment:

- How do you rotate signed artifacts when the cluster is airlocked (no outbound)? We need a clear ownership and handoff model.
- What operator-level scripts are expected to run inside the protected network vs. outboard?
- Can you provide a short checklist we can use during acceptance (scoped to artifact provenance, key handling, and rollback)?

I attached our baseline requirements — can you confirm Redwood's procedure and propose any gaps or automation we should expect?

Best,
Sally Park
Head of IT Operations
EdgeCorp

Attachments: edgecorp-airlock-requirements.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock deployment — artifact rotation and operator access questions

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed lightweight process attached.

1) Artifact rotation: We use an exportable signed-bundle model. Operator hands a signed USB (or courier-delivered HSM token image) to on-site admin, who verifies the signature against a pinned root cert kept in the cluster. For periodic rotations we publish deltas and a signed manifest; the cluster validates the manifest and applies only manifest-approved deltas.

2) Operator scripts: Anything that touches the private key material runs only on a sealed operator workstation (air-gapped laptop) with minimal tooling. Runtime health checks and metrics collection run inside the VPC but do not require egress; they emit locally-stored telemetry that can be swept out via signed bundle if requested.

3) Acceptance checklist: see attached operator-safety-checklist.xlsx — short items for provenance, signature verification, key custody, and rollback criteria.

Gaps we typically flag:
- If you require automated delta pulls from our hosted control plane, we'll need a courier path and signed manifests — fully manual otherwise.
- Operator training and the operator workstation hardening steps.

I attached a draft "artifact-rotation-matrix" that maps roles, artifacts, and handoff steps. Can Marissa and Priyom add the compliance language and confirm SLA implications?

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: artifact-rotation-matrix-v1.pdf; operator-safety-checklist.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sally Park <sally.park@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock deployment — artifact rotation and operator access questions

Sally, Jonas — quick compliance notes from my side:

- The signed-bundle + manifest approach is acceptable for our SOC2 controls provided we record the handoff event and store the manifest hashes in our audit log (we maintain an immutable ledger entry when a rotation publishes).
- We need EdgeCorp to designate a named operator (person) for KMS key custody and to confirm the physical chain-of-custody process for couriered tokens.
- Rollback criteria: define specific failure modes (signature mismatch, manifest tamper, unmet health check). Our default is automatic reject + operator alert; rollback requires a signed approval from the named operator and a secondary Redwood approval if past a safety window.

I added a compliance column to the matrix (see artifact-rotation-matrix-v1.pdf) and a short recommended change to the checklist: require operator proof-of-training (one-line cert) before first rotation.

Marissa
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sally Park <sally.park@edgecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock deployment — artifact rotation and operator access questions

Adding the ops POV and a small automation note:

- For delta application we suggest a two-phase apply: verify(manifest) -> stage -> smoke-checks -> commit. Stage and smoke-checks run locally; smoke-checks are a fixed set of deterministic tests we ship in the signed bundle. If smoke-checks fail, the bundle is quarantined on the host and an operator-run rollback command is made available (also in the signed bundle).
- We also recommend including a minimal JS/Go utility in the bundle to make verification reproducible (checksums + sig verify) — keep it single-binary and signed.
- Operator scripting guidance: no network-facing shells, no third-party package installs on the operator workstation beyond the signed utility.

I'm attaching the proposed "signed-key-ceremony-protocol.txt" with the exact verification command sequence for your operator. We can walk through it in a quick call.

— Priyom
Senior Manager, Private Deployments Ops

Attachments: signed-key-ceremony-protocol.txt
From: Sally Park <sally.park@edgecorp.com>

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick asks before we schedule the acceptance window: 

1) Can Redwood provide a one-page operator runbook (we prefer a single printed sheet) that our on-call can follow for the first two rotations?
2) Confirm whether the signed-bundle utility is reproducible on CentOS 7 (our sealed workstations run a hardened CentOS image).

If those two items are good, Procurement will issue the PO and Security will schedule the acceptance. Can we aim for a short call tomorrow to walk through the command sequence?

Best,
Sally
